extracted.intended_audience: advanced_undergraduate_or_graduate_students in algebraic number theory / elliptic curves (readers of lecture notes on FLT, Serre's conjecture, and Galois representations)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository lecture-notes style exposition covering algebraic number theory preliminaries, elliptic curve reduction and conductors, l-adic and mod-l Galois representations, Serre's conjecture, Ribet's level-lowering, and related lemmas used in the proof strategy for Fermat's Last Theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: σ is additive on torsion points
rubrics_metrics.description: σ is additive on the torsion points of a rational elliptic curve, i.e. σ(P + Q) = σ(P) + σ(Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: if three points P,Q,R are collinear on the curve then their images under σ are the same three points in some order, leading to σ(P+Q)=σ(P)+σ(Q). This shows the Galois action respects the group law on torsion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: σ permutes n-torsion points
rubrics_metrics.description: The function σ permutes the set of n-torsion points E[n] (since nσ(P)=σ(nP)=σ(O)=O, and σ is injective on torsion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because E[n] is finite and σ preserves torsion order and is injective, the action of σ on E[n] is a permutation (automorphism) of that finite set.

rubrics_metrics.name: l-adic Galois representation of an elliptic curve
rubrics_metrics.description: From the additive action of G_Q on each E[ℓ^n] compatible with multiplication-by-ℓ maps we obtain the Tate module and an ℓ-adic representation ρ_{E,ℓ}: Gal( Q̄ / Q ) → Aut(Tate_ℓ(E)) ≅ GL_2(Z_ℓ) ⊂ GL_2(Q_ℓ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard construction: the inverse limit of the ℓ^n-torsion with the Galois action gives a continuous representation into GL_2(Z_ℓ).

rubrics_metrics.name: mod ℓ Galois representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing the ℓ-adic representation mod ℓ yields the mod-ℓ representation ρ_{E,ℓ}: Gal( Q̄ / Q ) → GL_2(F_ℓ), i.e. the action of G_Q on E[ℓ] viewed as an F_ℓ-vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is equivalently the Galois action on the ℓ-division points; it is the reduction of the Tate module representation modulo ℓ.

rubrics_metrics.name: irreducibility of mod-P representation for Frey curve (Prop. 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For prime P ≥ 5 and E the Frey curve attached to x^P + y^P = z^P, the mod-P Galois representation ρ_{E,P} is irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is cited as Proposition 6 of [3] (the referenced source) and is used to apply modularity/level-lowering arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: irreducible ⇒ determinant = cyclotomic character (Prop. 11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ρ is irreducible then det ρ = χ (the cyclotomic character).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links irreducibility to the specific determinant expected for representations coming from elliptic curves (cyclotomic).

rubrics_metrics.name: determinant = cyclotomic ⇒ representation is odd (Prop. 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If det ρ = χ then ρ is odd (i.e. complex conjugation has determinant −1 in the 2-dimensional representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oddness is a necessary hypothesis in Serre's conjecture and in modularity-lifting contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's conjecture hypotheses and conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(F_p) be two-dimensional, irreducible, odd. Attach N, k, ε as in Serre. Then there exists a cuspidal eigenform f of weight k and level N with Fourier expansion f = Σ a_n q^n such that for all primes ℓ coprime to Np, ρ is unramified at ℓ and Tr(Frob_ℓ,ρ) = a_ℓ, det(Frob_ℓ,ρ) = ε(ℓ) ℓ^{k−1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serre gives explicit recipes to compute N (the conductor), k (the weight), and ε (the nebentypus) from ρ; verifying these properties for the Frey curve's representation is the program sketched.

rubrics_metrics.name: weight k = 2 criterion for Frey curve
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Frey curve, k=2 when ν_P(Δ) = 0 mod P (Proposition 11.7, citing Serre [3]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific condition used to get the expected weight for the modular form attached to the Frey representation; here ν_P(Δ) refers to the P-adic valuation of the discriminant.

rubrics_metrics.name: conductor (level) from Artin conductor
rubrics_metrics.description: The conductor N attached to ρ corresponds to the Artin conductor derived from local ramification data of the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once N is known and a modular form of level N exists, Ribet's level-lowering can be applied to reduce the level (e.g., eventually to level 2 in the Frey/Ribet strategy).

rubrics_metrics.name: unramified at ℓ
rubrics_metrics.description: A Galois representation is unramified at a prime ℓ if inertia at ℓ acts trivially (equivalently ρ(I_ℓ) = {1} in appropriate language); this allows a well-defined Frobenius element Frob_ℓ up to conjugacy in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unramifiedness at ℓ (for ℓ not dividing the conductor) is used to compare Tr(Frob_ℓ) and det(Frob_ℓ) with modular form coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius element and its role
rubrics_metrics.description: Frob_p (in finite fields or as an element of Galois groups) is x ↦ x^p on F_{p^k}; in representations one studies the conjugacy class of ρ(Frob_p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace and determinant of ρ(Frob_p) are well-defined (conjugacy-invariant) and carry arithmetic information (e.g., match Fourier coefficients of eigenforms).

rubrics_metrics.name: trace and determinant determine much of 2-dim representation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a two-dimensional representation, knowing trace and determinant of a matrix gives two invariants that determine eigenvalues and provide significant information about the matrix up to conjugacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence comparing Tr(Frob_ℓ) and det(Frob_ℓ) to modular form coefficients is powerful and central to Serre's conjecture and modularity correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: finite (finite flat) vs unramified
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite (or finite flat) at p is a condition defined in Serre [3]; for primes ℓ ≠ p, finite is equivalent to unramified. At p, being finite is the best analogue to unramified and implies many desirable consequences (including k = 2 in some settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes admit they do not fully unpack finite/finite-flat in group-scheme terms but emphasize its practical role in level-lowering arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frey-curve ramification specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve E, its mod p Galois representation is unramified outside pN and finite at p; specifically for the Frey curve the representation is unramified outside P and 2 (because Δ is a P-power).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This special ramification pattern is used to remove primes from the level via Ribet's theorem, leaving level 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ribet level-lowering condition
rubrics_metrics.description: When removing a prime from the level in Ribet's theorem, the representation must be finite/finite-flat at that removed prime (and conditions differ slightly for primes dividing N vs prime-factors of N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finiteness at removed primes is the technical hypothesis enabling level-lowering to a smaller N (e.g., to 2 in the Frey setup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius in finite fields (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In F_{p^k}, the Frobenius automorphism is Frob_p: x ↦ x^p; it is an automorphism fixing F_p and generates Gal(F_{p^k}/F_p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elementary properties: Frob_p preserves addition and multiplication; Fermat's little theorem shows it fixes F_p; used to define Frobenius classes in arithmetic Galois groups via reduction mod p.

rubrics_metrics.name: algebraic integer
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic integers A are complex numbers that are roots of monic polynomials with integer coefficients; the set A is a ring with A ∩ Q = Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic closure properties: sums, products, differences of algebraic integers are algebraic integers; roots of monic polynomials with algebraic-integer coefficients are algebraic integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: number field and ring of integers
rubrics_metrics.description: A number field K is a finite-degree extension of Q; its ring of integers O_K is K ∩ A (the algebraic integers in K), and O_K is a ring containing Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O_K is a finitely generated Z-module of rank [K:Q]; many arithmetic definitions (prime ideals, reduction) are phrased in terms of O_K.

rubrics_metrics.name: scaling to algebraic integer (Lemma 11.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any algebraic number α can be scaled by some non-zero integer m so that mα is an algebraic integer (multiply the minimal polynomial to clear denominators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used when choosing integral bases for O_K and in reduction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: trace Tr_{K/Q} definition and integrality
rubrics_metrics.description: For s ∈ K, Tr_{K/Q}(s) is the trace of the Q-linear map x ↦ s x on K. If s ∈ O_K then Tr_{K/Q}(s) ∈ Z; explicit formula relates trace to coefficient −a_{n−1}/a_n of the minimal polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to construct embeddings O_K → Z^n and to prove O_K is a finitely generated Z-module.

rubrics_metrics.name: O_K is a finitely generated Z-module (Theorem 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring of integers O_K is a finitely generated Z-module (in fact isomorphic to Z^n where n = [K:Q]), and a Z-basis of O_K is a Q-basis of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses traces to embed O_K injectively in Z^n and arguments about scaling arbitrary elements into O_K.

rubrics_metrics.name: residue fields at prime ideal are finite fields (Lemma 11.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p ⊂ O_K is a prime ideal lying over the rational prime p, then O_K/p ≅ F_{p^f} for some f ≥ 1 (i.e., residue field is finite extension of F_p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows primes in O_K are maximal and sets up the relation between decomposition/inertia groups and Galois groups of residue fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: action of Gal(K/Q) on O_K and primes (Theorem 11.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gal(K/Q) preserves O_K (algebraic integers) and permutes prime ideals of O_K; the action on primes lying over p is transitive (proof omitted here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies defining decomposition and inertia subgroups stabilizing a chosen prime of O_K.

rubrics_metrics.name: decomposition group D_p and inertia group I_p
rubrics_metrics.description: For a prime ideal p of O_K over p, D_p = {σ ∈ Gal(K/Q) | σ(p) = p} is the decomposition (stabiliser) group and I_p = {σ ∈ D_p | σ acts trivially on O_K/p} is the inertia subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These local subgroups measure how primes and residue fields behave under Galois action; they play a central role in defining ramification and Frobenius elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: local quotient is Galois group of residue field (Theorem 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a (natural) group isomorphism φ: D_p / I_p → Gal(O_K/p , F_p) (i.e., the decomposition group modulo inertia equals the Galois group of the residue field extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This isomorphism is used to pull back the Frobenius automorphism of the residue field to a well-defined class in D_p / I_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius element in global Galois (Definition 11.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Frob_p ∈ D_p / I_p as the preimage under φ^{-1} of the Frobenius automorphism of the residue field (x ↦ x^p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a representation is unramified at p, the image of this Frobenius class in the representation is a well-defined conjugacy class, used to compare with arithmetic invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: representation unramified at p (Definition 11.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation ρ of Gal(K/Q) is unramified at p if ρ(I_p) = {1} (in other words inertia acts trivially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to the property that Frobenius is defined (up to conjugacy) in the image of ρ and used in statements comparing ρ(Frob_p) with modular form coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: good reduction criterion for elliptic curves
rubrics_metrics.description: An elliptic curve E (minimal Weierstrass) has good reduction modulo p iff the discriminant Δ is non-zero modulo p; otherwise E has bad reduction, which is multiplicative if p ∤ c_4 and additive if p | c_4 (for p ≠ 2,3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical test: check Δ mod p and c_4 to determine reduction type; multiplicative reduction corresponds to nodal singularity, additive to cusp-like singularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: group law associativity on elliptic curve
rubrics_metrics.description: The addition defined on an elliptic curve is associative: (P+Q)+R = P+(Q+R) for all P,Q,R on the elliptic curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof can be given by geometric intersection arguments and Cayley–Bacharach-type theorems; associativity justifies treating E(Q) as an abelian group.

rubrics_metrics.name: definition of f_p and conductor N_E (Definitions 13.1 and 13.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each prime p define f_p = 0 if E has good reduction at p; f_p = 1 if multiplicative reduction at p; f_p = 2 (or 2+δ_p for p = 2,3) if additive reduction. The conductor N_E = ∏ p^{f_p}. For semistable E, all f_p ∈ {0,1} and N_E is a product of distinct primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conductor encodes local bad-reduction data; for semistable elliptic curves (no additive reduction) the conductor is squarefree.

rubrics_metrics.name: SL_n(R) and projective space basics
rubrics_metrics.description: SL_n(R) is the group of n×n matrices over ring R with determinant 1; projective space P^n(F) is (F^{n+1}\\{0})/∼ with scalar equivalence. These algebraic groups and spaces are the standard background for modular forms and related constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to set up modular group actions (e.g., SL_2(Z)) and the geometry of modular curves.
